repo: Phase 63 is pure backend crypto (sdk-core); frontend gate is skipped for all plan steps.
GSD commit helper consistently reports false-negatives — commits succeed despite misleading output; always verify via `git log`.
The API runs on port 3000 with a /health endpoint; CI polls it via `curl -fsS http://localhost:3000/health` in a bounded loop — mirror this pattern instead of `sleep N` in plan test steps.
Worktrees are avoided for this phase due to shared `folder.test.ts` between plans 63-01/63-04 and documented node_modules/api:generate leak pitfalls in this repo.
Plan 63-03 exposes 4 named Phase-64 seams inside the rotation engine.
The drift gate (stale .planning/codebase/ map) is non-blocking at plan time when CONTEXT.md and RESEARCH.md carry precise implementation-site references.

code.finding: `sleep 12` for API startup replaced with a bounded health-poll loop mirroring CI's curl pattern against http://localhost:3000/health.
Open Questions section required a `(RESOLVED)` marker and heading rename to clear plan-checker blocker — purely a formatting gate, not a content issue.

Template body must be manually filled with per-task verification map + `nyquist_compliant: true` after planning; step 5.5 leaves it empty by design, but plan-checker flags it as a warning if not filled before re-verify.

workflow: Plan-checker iteration 1 findings can be trivial formatting/tracking issues (not design flaws) — fix deterministically inline and re-run checker rather than replanning.
Sequential wave execution in the main worktree is safer than parallel worktrees when plans share test files or have barrel dependencies.
Drift gate non-blocking at plan time is the correct call when CONTEXT + RESEARCH files have up-to-date implementation references.
PATTERNS.md gets committed by the planner subagent, not the orchestrator — verify it lands before spawning the checker.

friction: GSD commit helper false-negatives on every commit required a `git log` verification step each time, adding noise throughout the session.
Plan-checker iteration 1 flagged 3 issues requiring a read-fix-recommit-recheck loop; all were formatting/artifact gaps rather than plan design problems.
VALIDATION.md requires a two-pass fill: skeleton written at step 5.5, body populated only after all plan task IDs and automated commands are known — easy to miss.
